The best of Google, right on your devices

Google Mobile Services brings Google’s most popular apps and APIs to your Android devices.

Get Started

Google's most popular apps, all in one place

Google Mobile Services (GMS) is a collection of Google applications and APIs that help support functionality across devices. These apps work together seamlessly to ensure your device provides a great user experience right out of the box.

Google Search

The Google app is the fastest, easiest way for users to find what they need on the web and on their Android devices.1

Google Chrome

Google Chrome for mobile lets users browse fast while saving up to 50% of data usage while browsing.1

YouTube

With the YouTube app, users can watch the latest videos, subscribe to channels they love, share with friends, and watch on any device.

Google Play Store

With more than 1 million apps, the world's largest collection of eBooks, millions of songs and thousands of movies, Google Play has something for everyone

Explore more GMS apps:

Add GMS to your devices

While the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) provides common, device-level functionalities such as email and calling, GMS is not part of AOSP. GMS is only available through a license with Google and delivers a holistic set of popular apps and cloud-based services. Note that GMS apps can vary based on country availability and requirements.2

With GMS, the choice is yours

You can choose to pre-install GMS apps on a device-by-device basis, as well as pre-install your own apps, apps from third party publishers, or other AOSP apps. Of course, customers can also install any apps they choose from the Google Play Store

Ensuring compatibility, right out of the box

We ask GMS partners to pass a simple compatibility test and adhere to our compatibility requirements for their Android devices. In turn, your users enjoy greater app reliability and continuity.

Learn more about device compatibility

Say hello to our partners

Hundreds of approved manufacturers already provide a great out-of-the-box-experience by collaborating with Google

See our partners

1 The Google app and Chrome are not included in GMS for devices dispatched in the EEA. Enquire for a separate licence.

2 Please use the geo-availability spreadsheet to check the available applications and required GMS apps for each country.

Use Find Hub Compatible devices Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Find Hub  turns ‘lost’ into ‘found’—helping you locate tags, devices, and connect with family and friends quickly and safely. Find Connect Protect FAQ Find. Find. Find. Easily locate your devices on a map. You can find them even if they are offline¹ or on silent. Look on a map Play sound Pinpoint location Locate lost luggage Look on a map Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Pull up the map view to see where your belonging was last located. You can even get directions if it is not nearby. Find my device on Find Hub Play sound Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video You can tap “Play sound” to ring a device, making it easier to find if it fell behind your bed or buried beneath some pillows. Tap “Find nearby” to see its precise location. Find Hub makes sure your location sharing automatically ends when you want so your privacy always stays in your hands. Share location on Find Hub Share via satellite No connection? No worries. Share your location, live, with friends and family over satellite using Find Hub on Android. 4 Share location on Find Hub Share a location Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Play silent looping video Pause silent looping video Share your location with friends and family to make coordinating meetups easier. You choose who can see your location and for how long, while also seeing their names, distance, and battery levels. 4 Share location on Find Hub Protect. Protect. Protect. Protect your personal data and privacy with robust security features and proactive safety alerts. Encrypted for privacy. Device location data on the Find Hub network is encrypted using the PIN, pattern, or password for your Android device. 5 Secure, lock, or erase from anywhere. You can add a PIN, pattern, or secure and lock a device to help keep your data safe. Your privacy is our priority. Unknown tracker alerts. For your safety, your Bluetooth-enabled Android phone can send you unknown tracker alerts if it detects an unfamiliar Bluetooth tag traveling with you. Some extra help from a global network. Find Hub uses a global network of Android devices to locate your belongings almost anywhere. Find more than just phones. From earbuds to luggage, Find Hub lets you locate all kinds of items in the same app. Look for the “Works with Android” badge to see compatible accessories. Shop partners Wearables Headphones Tracking Tags Explore compatible accessories. Shop partners or look for the “Works with Android” badge to see which accessories are compatible. FAQs How do I find an Android device using Find Hub? Go to the Help Centre to get step-by-step instructions on getting set up with Find Hub. What Android version is required to use Find Hub? Android phones with OS 6 and above can use the Find Hub app. You can also access the app in a web browser on laptops and tablets. The Find Hub network requires Android phones with OS 9 and above. What phones and accessories, like tracking tags, work with Find Hub? Android accessories like earbuds, headphones, tracking tags, tablets, watches, smart luggages, and more may be compatible. Look for the “Works with Android” badge on accessories that work with Find Hub. See the full list here. How do I share my device locations with friends and family? You can add friends and family to shared items like a tablet or house keys with a tag attached. For more info on sharing device locations, go to the Help Centre . Can I use Find Hub to find my phone (e.g. Pixel, Samsung, and/or other Android phones)? You can find Android devices with OS 9 and up with the Find Hub network. Go to android.com/find to locate them on the Web or use the Find Hub app on a friend’s phone or tablet by signing into the app as a guest. How do I mark my phone as lost? You can use the “secure device” option to lock your device screen with your PIN, pattern, or password. If you do not have a lock, you can set one. To help someone return your device to you, you can add a message or phone number to the lock screen. How do I share my location with my friends or family? Open the  Find Hub app . Navigate to the "People" tab on the bottom right. Click the "+" icon. Select the duration of time you wish to share your location. Select the contacts you want to share your location with. Tap "Share". Go to the Help Centre for more ways to share your location with friends or family on Find Hub. How do I stop sharing my location with someone? Tap on the user you would like to stop sharing with. Tap the “Stop sharing” button. From the confirmation dialog, you can either: Cancel: Your share stays and you go back to the details page. Confirm: If the user is also sharing with you, you will stay on the contact detail page and the button will no longer be blue. You can start a new share if you want. If you are the only one sharing, you will be sent back to the list of shares. Go to the Help Centre for more ways to stop sharing your location with friends or family on Find Hub. Can I track lost Pixel Buds? Yes, you can track your lost Pixel Buds using Google's Find Hub. The Find Hub app will show their last known location on a map, and if they are nearby, you can make them ring to help you find them. Can I track my Android tablet’s location? Absolutely, you can track your lost Android tablet's location with Google's Find Hub. The Find Hub allows you to see your Samsung, Pixel, or other Android tablet on a map and even lock it remotely for security. Can I find my Wear OS watch using my phone? Yes, your phone is the key to finding your lost Android or Samsung watch. Use the Find Hub app to see your watch's last known location or make it ring loudly to help you locate it when it is nearby.
